gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 14 build gate now needs one more bounded module so the skbuff study lane becomes reviewable without widening into a fake port.
The existing make target keeps the skbuff bridge lane runnable with the same bounded discipline as the other Phase 14 studies.

The first honest skbuff foothold is a boundary map around __alloc_skb(), napi_alloc_skb(), skb_clone(), pskb_expand_head(), __skb_checksum_complete(), skb_segment(), and consume_skb(), with explicit stay-in-C decisions where shared-data ownership and teardown are still too coupled to refcounts and destructors.
A dedicated Phase 14 test gate is the smallest truthful way to lock the new boundary map to its manifest and keep later runs from drifting into fake implementation claims.
The slice note records the exact boundary-map posture so the lane does not overstate symbol cataloging as skbuff ownership.
The survey note compares the 7,476-line skbuff anchor, its 5,467-line public header, and a nearby datagram user against the new bridge so future runs stay honest about what still belongs in C.

The bridge now carries a small lifetime audit outline around dataref splits, pskb_expand_head() clone-or-reallocate handoff, destructor_arg and frag-list teardown, and checksum or GSO metadata coupling so Zigux can name the ownership risks without claiming live allocator, refcount, or destructor control.

The bridge now separates checksum-complete state around __skb_checksum_complete() and skb_checksum_complete_unset() so the lane can name skb->csum, skb->ip_summed, skb->csum_valid, and skb->csum_complete_sw without claiming live checksum-state ownership.

The next honest skbuff step is a tighter study of skb_segment(), skb_orphan_frags(), and skb_zerocopy_clone() so the lane can document how frag ownership and checksum metadata move across segmentation without weakening the current stay-in-C posture.

Live skbuff allocation, dataref transitions, checksum-state caching, destructor-driven teardown, frag-list ownership, and GSO segmentation remain blocked until Phase 14 has much stronger stay-in-C evidence and still keeps those mechanisms in the existing C implementation.
